_role: The autonomy loop's POSTURE — the only thing a cycle reads before deciding whether to start (architecture §4.2 step 1). Written by the budget governor, read by research/autonomy/health.py. It is state, not a plan: what the loop is currently doing, never what it should do.
_why_this_lives_in_git: §9 property 2: state lives in git, never in context. A killed session loses nothing but its turn — the next fired cycle re-reads this file and the ledger and continues. There is no resume protocol because there is no in-context state worth resuming.
_backoff_level_means: 0 = full cadence and width. Raised by a cycle that ended without a receipt, lowered by a clean one (§9 property 3). Two dials hang off it: cycle interval (4 h -> 8 h -> 24 h) and subagent width (5 -> 2 -> 1). At level >= 2 the cycle takes only `fetch` and `regrade` items, which are dispatch-and-exit and consume no Claude budget — the loop keeps making progress on a spent budget instead of stopping.
_backoff_since_utc_means: The stamp the governor writes IN THE SAME WRITE that raises `backoff_level`. Null while the level is 0. It exists because §5.2's `budget_recovering` is entirely a DURATION ('backoff > 0 for > 24 h'), and a level with no start time cannot be graded — health.py reports that case as `unmeasured`, never as ok.
_subagent_width_means: ⛔ THE UNIT IS MAXIMUM CONCURRENT SUBAGENTS, AND IT HAD NEVER BEEN STATED — which is why the cap was unenforceable rather than merely unenforced. Architecture §9 calls it 'parallel width' and the cycle contract says 'launch them in ONE message so they run concurrently', so CONCURRENT is the reading both texts support and it is now written down. The 107-agent incident (40 completed, 67 errored, synthesis lost) was one fan-out launched together, i.e. a concurrent width of 107 against this cap of 5. ⛔ WIDTH MOVES LAST AND MOVES DOWN FASTER THAN IT MOVES UP: 5 -> 2 -> 1 by backoff_level, because the architecture records it as the dial that failed catastrophically. ⚠ WHAT THIS DIAL DOES NOT GOVERN, SAID PLAINLY RATHER THAN LEFT TO BE DISCOVERED: the TOTAL number of subagents a cycle may spend serially. A cycle running 5, waiting, then 5 more, twenty times over, never exceeds this cap and can still exhaust a weekly budget. That total is UNGOVERNED and no number is invented for it here — inventing one would be a remembered figure standing in for a measurement (CLAUDE.md §4). The measurement that would settle it is `utilisation_denominator`, which is null until a window flip is OBSERVED.
_max_cycles_per_session_means: ⛔ THE SESSION-SHAPE CAP, ADDED 2026-08-26 AFTER THE RULE FAILED IN THE WILD. The skill's §3 says a full hardening cycle is a SPAWNED SESSION, not more work in the current one, because context is the resource that silently runs out. Measured that day: one interactive session ran CYC-0005 and CYC-0006 end to end, compacted 23 times and reached a 7.6 MB transcript, and the rule never fired because it lives in a skill that was never loaded ("name":"Skill" appears 0 times in that session). 2 is a CAP, not a target: one cycle per session is the intended shape and the second is slack for a cycle that turns out to have a small follow-on. The third is the signal that the driver should have spawned. ⚠ It bounds CYCLES, which is a proxy for context and not context itself — a single enormous cycle passes it. The proxy is used because receipts already carry `session_id` and nothing in this repository can read a context window, and an imperfect measurement that fires beats a perfect one that does not exist.
_start_point_means: §9.2's start point, and it is DELIBERATELY BELOW TARGET: the controller's first job is to measure the ceiling by approaching it, not to find it by hitting it. Dials move in this order of preference — cycle frequency first (it is smooth), then items per cycle, and only then subagent width. Width moves last and moves down faster than it moves up: the 107-agent fan-out that hit the weekly cap (40 completed, 67 errored, synthesis lost) was a WIDTH failure, not a depth one.
_utilisation_target_means: trimcrae, 2026-08-26 (D3): 'about 80% of the max budget', leaving ~20% as his interactive headroom. A target for the CONTROLLER, never a floor for the WORK — an empty queue means an idle loop, not make-work to hit a number.
_utilisation_denominator_means: UNKNOWN, and it stays null until a window flip is OBSERVED. `rate_limit_info` returns a verdict (`status`, `rateLimitType`, `resetsAt`, `isUsingOverage`), not a quota, so how much of the window REMAINS is not readable (§9.1). The denominator is therefore CALIBRATED, not assumed: the loop records the consumption at which `status` last flipped away from `allowed`, and THAT observed figure becomes this number. Inventing one would put a fabricated denominator underneath every utilisation reading the controller takes — an absent reading is not a reading of absence (CLAUDE.md §4), and §9.2 is explicit that the loop says UNKNOWN rather than guessing.

last_limit_flip._means: The first OBSERVED flip of rate_limit_info.status away from `allowed`. Recorded by CYC-0088-f7394a99 from a child session's own rate_limit_info. ⛔ IT SUPPLIES NO DENOMINATOR: `allowed_warning` is a verdict, not a quota, so `utilisation_denominator` stays null. Recording it CONSTRAINS the loop and loosens nothing.
last_limit_flip.observed_consumption: UNKNOWN — the endpoint returns a verdict, not a remaining fraction

It is the calibration event for `utilisation_denominator` above. Null = never observed, which is why the denominator is still UNKNOWN.
_isUsingOverage_is_not_headroom: Overage means the work has crossed from the flat-rate subscription into METERED DOLLARS, and CLAUDE.md §5's 'engineering effort is free' stops being true at that moment. A cycle that observes it treats it as a spend event under §7 trigger 2 — it is watched, never celebrated.

budget_hold._means: ⛔⛔ A BUDGET HOLD IS NOT A BACKOFF, AND THE GOVERNOR HAD NO WAY TO SAY SO UNTIL NOW. `backoff_level` is defined as a FAILURE counter — raised by a cycle that ended without a receipt, LOWERED BY A CLEAN ONE. So a level raised for budget reasons is undone by the first cycle that goes well, which is exactly the cycle you least want to license the next six. This block is the missing half: it pins a FLOOR under `backoff_level` that a clean cycle may not decrement through, and it carries its own reason and expiry.
budget_hold._SUSPENDED_FOR_THE_SPRINT_2026_09_01:
⛔⛔ LIFTED BY THE PERSON WHO SET IT, FOR A NAMED AND BOUNDED WINDOW — NOT BY THE LOOP, AND NOT BECAUSE THE HOLD WAS INCONVENIENT. `_review_after_utc_means` and architecture §10.4 both forbid the loop from lifting its own budget hold; neither is bent here, because the lift is his. He set the hold on 2026-08-29 with "Adjust the rate at which this autonomous system consumes tokens accordingly"; on 2026-09-01 he removed its entire premise — the window that was 71% spent has RESET, and the replacement instruction is the exact opposite of the one that set the hold: spend it, because it expires unspent.

⛔ AND IT IS SUSPENDED, NOT DELETED. `reactivates_utc` below is the window boundary the instrument reports. Past it the pre-sprint posture is the DEFAULT again and a fresh reading is required to loosen it — the ladder rule is untouched: a dial moves down faster than up.
budget_hold._reactivates_utc_means: ⛔ THE SPRINT AUTHORISATION ENDS WHEN THE WINDOW DOES, AND THAT IS AN OBSERVED BOUNDARY RATHER THAN A GUESS — `last_limit_flip.resets_at_epoch`, corroborated by his own 14-hour figure to within half an hour. A cycle starting after this stamp with no fresh reading restores `active: true`, `floor_backoff_level: 2` and the pre-sprint posture recorded in `declared_posture._pre_sprint_posture_to_restore`. ⚠ IT IS NOT AN EXPIRY INTO FULL CADENCE: past the stamp the loop is at the PRE-SPRINT posture, and only a fresh utilisation reading may loosen it again. The whole point of a 14-hour grant is that hour 15 is a new week's budget, spent from zero.

budget_hold._why_width_is_12_and_not_107:
⛔⛔ THE 107-AGENT INCIDENT IS WHY THIS IS A NUMBER AND NOT "MASSIVELY PARALLEL". 40 completed, 67 errored, THE SYNTHESIS LOST — and the loss was not the errors, it was that the 40 successes had nowhere to land, so their findings were recovered by hand out of `journal.jsonl`. Two of that failure's three causes are addressed here rather than hoped away:
(1) ⭐ THE CAUSE THAT IS GONE: it exhausted an ALREADY-SPENT weekly window. This window has just reset and its whole content is authorised to be spent. That is why 12 is defensible today and would not be tomorrow.
(2) ⭐ THE CAUSE THAT IS ENGINEERED AROUND: a lost synthesis. EVERY seat in this sprint writes its findings to its OWN file under `research/autonomy/sprint-2026-09-01/` BEFORE it returns, so a seat that errors on the way home costs its own work and nothing else, and a driver that dies loses no finding at all. The durable artifact is the deliverable; the returned summary is a convenience.
(3) ⛔ THE CAUSE THAT IS STILL REAL, AND IS WHY THIS IS 12 RATHER THAN 40: one fan-out launched together is one failure domain. The sprint runs WAVES of ≤12 with disjoint file ownership, never one launch of everything.
⚠ AND WIDTH STILL MOVES DOWN FASTER THAN UP: this is a 14-hour ceiling with a stamp on it, not a new resting value.
